robot: duck-sim (backlash scene, set v10, microduck 094d4bb4, microduck_rl 0daab160)

camera.about: The simulated camera's fidelity (RFC-0016, duck_lab/nav/sim_camera.py): guesses, not measured, until a real camera and detector are. Field of view and range of recognition, the probability of recognising an object in view (falling to half at range), range noise in proportion, bearing noise in degrees, how often it looks.

measured: 2026-11-14, robots/duck/sim/probes/odom_vs_truth.py (straight walks, 3 x 8 s per speed, truth = body server trunk) and robots/duck/sim/odom_scale.py over ~41 m of navigation logs (0.909). Re-measured 2026-11-19 on the same probe, 4 x 8 s per speed: truth/odometry 0.856 at 0.2, 0.893 at 0.25, 0.913 at 0.3, 0.940 at 0.4, each within the runs' own spread (0.84-0.88 at 0.2), so the table stands. In navigation (robots/duck/sim/odom_by_speed.py, 440 runs, belief over truth with `scale` alone): 0.995 at 0.3 straight (826.8 m), 0.986 at 0.3 turning (111.8 m), 0.986 at 0.2 on arcs (7.9 m); no straight 0.2 walk is in those runs.
why: robotd's odometry reads ~10 % long in the simulator and mapd builds its map from it; the navigator scales odometry, mapd's poses and mapd's grid by this factor (operator, 2026-11-14: options 2 and 3). The simulator's odometry reads longer the slower the duck walks (K8), so the navigator's own dead reckoning between fixes scales each step by the table's value at the speed commanded while a straight walk (a turn under straight_rad_s, the navigator's slow_yaw_rad_s) was walked; `scale` stays the map's and mapd's pose's metres, and corrects pivots and arcs (arcs at 0.2 m/s measured right with it, 0.986). A real duck gets its own measurement (phase 5). Remove when robotd or mapd corrects it upstream.

pivot.measured: 2026-11-16. A turn on the spot creeps the way the duck faces: 0.27 m per full turn, p95 0.54 m, from the truth over the challenge course (robots/duck/sim/probes/turn_drift.py). robots/duck/sim/probes/pivot_counter.py, ch5-s3, a half turn to the right at 0.8 rad/s, one sample each: moved 0.111 m with vx 0, 0.058 m with -0.035, 0.026 m with -0.06.
pivot.why: a U-turn in a 60 cm corridor (challenge 5) ended 8-11 cm toward the side it turned to and was refused for no room to turn: 6/10 with vx 0. With -0.06 sent during a pivot: 10/10, twice; challenges 1, 3, 8, 9 10/10, challenge 2 9/10 (seed 5 stalled after a detour that began before any pivot; 3/3 on a rerun). A side-choice before a large turn (from the map, then from a head glance) was tried first: 6/10 and 3/10, dropped. The real duck pivots backward by upstream (RFC-0008 §4) and keeps 0 until its pivot is measured.

tof.measured: 2026-11-16. Range: the simulator's tof.py casts unit rays (mj_ray) and reports the hit distance along each, so readings are radial. Pitch: robots/duck/sim/probes/floor_fit.py over the challenge course's 40 flat-floor runs, the offset (0 to 4 deg in 0.5 deg steps with radial readings, and the real duck's 3 deg axial) that puts the recorded floor returns at floor height; 2.5 deg radial places them at +5.5 to -3.7 mm from 0.3 to 0.9 m (mean |error| 2.8 mm, the smallest), 0 deg radial 16 to 32 mm high (23.2), 3 deg axial 6 to 18 mm low (14.6). The servo joints alone (tof_truth.py, which leaves the model's passive backlash hinges at 0) put the optical axis 3.0 deg less steep than 3 deg believed: the extra ~2.5 deg is not in the servo angles, most likely the head sagging on its backlash hinges (not measured directly).
tof.why: with the real duck's values (3 deg, axial) the cliff check placed the floor up to 2 cm too low and, with the head near level (the walk's first second, the neck pitched up ~13 deg), stopped for drops that were not there: 131 frames and 8 cliff stops in the challenge course's 40 runs on flat floor (robots/duck/sim/probes/cliff_replay.py). 0 deg also removed them but by placing the floor too high, which made the check blind to the first 2-3 cm of any drop. The real duck keeps mapd's 3 deg and axial ranges (cliff.py's defaults); whether the real sensor's ranges are axial is not checked here.
